title: Evidence of the kind the claim makes
statement: Accept a claim only on evidence of its kind, runtime evidence for behaviour, independent review of the exact text for meaning, access testing for access, however much weaker evidence agrees.
detail: The student-course quality standard asks of every requirement verdict whether the evidence type matches the claim: runtime claims use runtime evidence, semantic claims independent semantic review, access claims access testing, and state and event claims a reconciliation of recorded behaviour (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/quality/golden-student-course/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd`, lines 97-102). Its failure signals are static prose used for runtime behaviour, self-review used as independent judgment and screenshots used for accessibility, and it holds that a weaker evidence type cannot be upgraded by confidence or repetition (lines 103-104). The Grade 5 instruction-review profile applies it: presentation claims need runtime evidence because source files or tests alone cannot prove them, and semantic claims need the exact learner-facing text in context (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/courses/g5-reading/review/generated/instruction-review-profile.json`, lines 154-155).

evidence.quote: Runtime claims use runtime evidence; semantic claims use independent semantic review; access claims use access testing;
Failure signals: Static prose used for runtime behavior; self-review used as independent judgment; screenshots used for accessibility.
A weaker evidence type cannot be upgraded by confidence or repetition.
Presentation claims require runtime evidence; source files or tests alone cannot prove them.
Semantic claims require exact learner-facing text in context; documentation is not behavior evidence.
